statement: Specialize quantize_q8_1_1d on gfx90a so each lane quantizes eight contiguous values using two float4 loads and each 32-value Q8_1 block is handled by four lanes instead of the current eight-lane float4 mapping. This preserves Q8_1 types, metadata, and output layout while halving block groups and removing one subgroup-reduction stage; the 18.63% hotspot should fall enough to improve tg128 decode.

In the gfx90a specialization of quantize_q8_1_1d, replace the ten width-32 generic __shfl_xor_sync operations used by the max and sum reductions with immediate __builtin_amdgcn_ds_swizzle XOR patterns for offsets 16, 8, 4, 2, and 1. Preserve the existing reduction order and non-CDNA2 fallback, yielding bit-identical Q8_1 blocks while avoiding dynamic lane-index formation and ds_bpermute in an 18.63% hotspot.

In the gfx90a path of quantize_q8_1_1d, retain the champion's floating-point sum reduction and make_half2(d, sum) metadata exactly, but convert pairs of scaled values with packed round-to-nearest f32-to-i16 operations and pack the resulting in-range int8 values with v_perm before the existing stores. This removes scalar conversion and packing VALU work from the top 19.26% decode hotspot without changing Q8_1 arithmetic, metadata, or type dispatch.

In vec_dot_q4_K_q8_1_impl_vmmq, use the existing Q8_1 ds.y block-sum sidecar for the Q4_K minimum-term contribution instead of recomputing each Q8 byte sum with two dp4a operations. This removes integer dot-product work from the type-12 MMVQ route, which accounts for 35.49% of decode device time.

In ggml_cuda_mul_mat_vec_q, cache the quantize_q8_1_1d result within each graph-capture generation, keyed by src1 producer identity, shape, and required quant type, so Q/K/V and gate/up MMVQ consumers reuse one Q8_1 activation buffer instead of launching identical quantization kernels; this targets the 19.22% decode hotspot without changing quant types or arithmetic.

In vec_dot_q4_K_q8_1, interleave two independent packed-int8 v_dot4 accumulator chains and combine them after each Q4_K scale group, preserving the existing Q8 sum-sidecar correction while shortening the serialized dot-product dependency path in Q4_K mul_mat_vec_q kernels that account for about 33% of device time.

In vec_dot_q6_K_q8_1_impl_vmmq, replace repeated shift-and-mask reconstruction of packed Q6_K weights from ql/qh with gfx90a __builtin_amdgcn_perm byte extraction, preserving the existing Q8_1 scale and sum arithmetic and targeting no more than 64 VGPRs. This should reduce integer unpack work in the type-14 mul_mat_vec_q kernels, which account for 16.66% of decode device time.

Fuse Q8_1 activation quantization into the Q4_K mul_mat_vec_q decode kernel, using __ballot(1) for each divergent kbx iteration and the existing masked-shuffle layer to preserve Q8_1 scale/sum arithmetic, four-lane XOR reductions, and odd-block behavior. This removes separate quantize_q8_1_1d launches and intermediate global-memory traffic while leaving activation type selection and dispatch tables unchanged; the live profile still assigns 18.99% to quantization and 33.34% to the Q4_K MMVQ route.

Refactor vec_dot_q6_K_q8_1 so each scalar ql/qh chunk is loaded once, immediately contributes both its low- and high-nibble Q6 values, and dies before the next chunk is loaded. Unlike the rejected lexical-scope factoring, this removes the vector vl/vh values spanning both phases without adding global reads, while preserving lane mapping, Q8_1 type, scale arithmetic, and the final reduction. Shorter packed-operand live ranges should bring the type-14 MMVQ specialization to at most 64 VGPRs, raising gfx90a occupancy from 6 to 8 waves across 16.68% of decode device time.

In the gfx90a two-half-wave quantize_q8_1_1d specialization, replace the xor-1 and xor-2 ds_swizzle stages for absmax and sum with exact quad-permute v_max_f32_dpp and v_add_f32_dpp operations. Mark the inline assembly volatile and place an AMDGCN convergent wave barrier after the staged reductions and before the divergent iqs > 0 return, ensuring every partner lane completes the cross-lane updates. Preserve reduction order, rounding, Q8_1 scale/sum arithmetic, and output layout while removing four DS instructions per block from the 18.99% decode hotspot.

Fuse Q8_1 activation quantization into the gfx90a Q4_K mul_mat_vec_q decode specialization. For each divergent kbx iteration, derive the participating lanes with __ballot(1) and use the existing masked-shuffle reductions while preserving Q8_1 scale and sum arithmetic, rounding, four-lane XOR reduction order, odd-block handling, activation type selection, and dispatch tables. Removing the separate quantize_q8_1_1d launches and intermediate global-memory traffic attacks the 18.99% quantization hotspot feeding the 33.34% Q4_K MMVQ route.

Fuse Q8_1 activation quantization into the gfx90a Q4_K mul_mat_vec_q decode specialization. Derive a participating-lane mask with __ballot(1) for each divergent kbx iteration and use the existing masked-shuffle reductions, preserving Q8_1 scale/sum arithmetic, rounding, odd-block behavior, activation type selection, and dispatch tables. Removing separate quantize_q8_1_1d launches and intermediate global-memory traffic targets the 19.22% quantization hotspot feeding the 33.22% Q4_K MMVQ route.

In the existing gfx90a two-half-wave quantize_q8_1_1d specialization, replace only the xor-1 and xor-2 ds_swizzle plus VALU stages for absmax and sum with exact quad-permute v_max_f32_dpp and v_add_f32_dpp operations. Keep xor-4, xor-8, and xor-16 unchanged, use volatile inline assembly, and place a convergent AMDGCN wave barrier before the divergent iqs > 0 return. This preserves reduction order, Q8_1 rounding, scale/sum arithmetic, lane ownership, activation type, and output layout while removing four DS instructions from the 19.22% decode hotspot.

Fuse Q8_1 activation quantization into every gfx90a Q4_K ncols_dst=1 mul_mat_vec_q specialization, including gate-fused, non-gated, and other small_k variants, so the full 33.22% combined Q4_K MMVQ route no longer launches quantize_q8_1_1d or reads its intermediate buffer. For each divergent k-block iteration, obtain participating lanes with HIP __ballot(1) or CUDA __ballot_sync(__activemask(), 1), then use masked shuffle reductions while preserving Q8_1 rounding, scale and sum arithmetic, four-lane XOR order, odd-block handling, activation type selection, dot-product order, and output layout.

In ggml_cuda_op_mul_mat_vec_q, route every gfx90a Q4_K ncols_dst=1 specialization through the existing inline-Q8_1 path by passing the original F32 src1_ddf_i input and setting inline_q8_1=true, including the standard path that currently passes src1_ddq_i. Each active k-block reproduces the existing Q8_1 rounding, scale, correction sum, masked reductions, odd-block handling, and output order locally, eliminating the separate quantize_q8_1_1d launch and intermediate-buffer traffic from the combined Q4_K decode route without changing activation type or dispatch-table entries.

Reapply the preserved 01893a36 delta atop the current champion: carry each Q8_1 block's post-rounding correction sum as a compact sidecar and consume it directly in the Q4_K dual-dot path, eliminating redundant half-to-float conversion and shortening live ranges across the combined 33.28% Q4_K mul_mat_vec_q route without changing activation quantization, dispatch, layout, or reduction order.

Add a gfx90a-specific Q6_K ncols_dst=1 launch entry that changes mul_mat_vec_q from two waves to one. At n_embd=1536, each row has six Q6_K blocks and one 64-lane wave covers two blocks per iteration, yielding three fully active iterations; the current two-wave CTA covers four blocks and then runs its second iteration half-empty, followed by an LDS cross-wave reduction and barrier. The one-wave specialization removes that tail underutilization and the cross-wave reduction while leaving quantization, dot products, accumulation order within each lane, and dispatch types unchanged.

In vec_dot_q4_K_q8_1_dual, have each existing gfx90a four-lane group load the Q4_K superblock's packed dm half2 once in its leader and DPP-broadcast those exact 32 bits before the unchanged scale/min unpack and dual-dot arithmetic. This removes three redundant dm loads and their address calculations from the hottest 15.21% small_k gate-only Q4_K route without changing quantization, dispatch, accumulation order, or output layout.

surface: ggml/src/ggml-cuda/vecdotq.cuh Q4_K batch-1 mul_mat_vec_q decode path
statement: In vec_dot_q4_K_q8_1_impl_vmmq, have each existing gfx90a four-lane group load the Q4_K superblock's packed dm half2 once in its leader and DPP-broadcast those exact 32 bits to the other three lanes before the unchanged scale/min unpack and dot arithmetic. This removes three redundant dm loads and their address calculations per group on high-share Q4_K decode routes without changing activation quantization, dispatch, conversions, accumulation order, or output layout.

In vec_dot_q6_K_q8_1, specialize the gfx90a Q6_K path so the packed ggml_cuda_dp4a operations within each fixed-scale group alternate between two independent int32 accumulators, then add those accumulators before the existing float scale and accumulation step. This breaks the serial dp4a dependency chain while preserving the exact integer group sum and existing floating-point accumulation order; the schedule is accepted only if llvm-objdump keeps the kernel at <=64 VGPR with no spills.

In mul_mat_vec_q, move bias/index loads and their derived values from the prologue to immediately before the epilogue for the Q4_K bias-only specializations, shortening register live ranges across the dot-product loop without changing arithmetic or type selection. These specializations account for 21.72% of device time, so reduced VGPR pressure or spills should improve decode throughput.

Baseline gfx90a descriptors allocate 39 and 37 VGPR for the two Q4_K bias-only specializations, so the rejected 64-VGPR crossing does not exist. Instead, pack four 16-lane row groups per wave for CDNA2 Q4_K ncols=1 small-k kernels, producing eight rows per 128-thread CTA instead of four. Since QI4_K/VDR is 16 lanes, four K partitions can be recombined in the current reduction order, preserving numerics while halving CTA and per-row lane overhead across the 18.71% and 16.08% hotspots.

In vec_dot_q6_K_q8_1, keep unpacked Q6_K values in their unsigned 0..63 representation, accumulate signed dp4a products directly, and subtract 32 times a dp4a-computed activation subgroup sum before applying each Q6_K scale. This preserves the integer dot product while removing packed per-element biasing and sign-conversion instructions from the two Q6_K kernels that total 20.35% of device time.

For 1536-element rows, launch rms_norm_f32 with 512 threads and have each lane accumulate three strided elements before the existing wave reduction. This cuts the workgroup from 16 to 8 wavefronts and halves cross-wave reduction and synchronization work; the mechanism is reduced reduction overhead, not increased residency.

Specialize rms_norm_f32 for the contracted 1536-element rows to use a 256-thread workgroup with each lane processing coalesced float4 chunks, then reduce the sum of squares across four wave64 wavefronts. This replaces the current 1024-thread, 16-wave workgroup and its larger cross-wave reduction with fewer scheduled waves and less LDS/barrier work while preserving the existing normalization formula.

Specialize the gfx90a wave64 final reduction in mul_mat_vec_q: use DPP row-shift adds for the four intra-16-lane stages and retain lane permutations only for the cross-row combines, replacing most HIP shuffle operations that compile to ds_bpermute. This removes LDS-path permutation latency and scoreboard waits from the Q4_K and Q6_K kernels that dominate decode.

In vec_dot_q6_K_q8_1_impl_vmmq, after merging ql and qh into packed unsigned 6-bit bytes, convert four weights at once to the exact signed Q6_K values q-32 with ((uint32_t(q6) + 0x60606060u) ^ 0x80808080u), then feed that packed word directly to the existing dp4a path. Since every lane is in [0,63], the addition cannot carry between bytes; this removes scalar subtract/sign-extension instructions and shortens temporary live ranges on the Q6_K route, which accounts for 20.35% of the profile.

Specialize the gfx90a D=128, ncols=1, F16 K/V path so each lane keeps its computed softmax weight in a register and broadcasts it to the existing 8-lane V groups with a wave64 shuffle, converting to half at the same point as today. This replaces the hot-loop KQ LDS store and repeated LDS reads without changing score mapping, V parallelism, or numerical precision.

Specialize rms_norm_f32 for ncols=1536 to launch 512 threads, with each thread loading and writing indices tid, tid+512, and tid+1024 in fp32. This halves the block_reduce half-wave partials from 32 to 16 versus the profiled 1024-thread kernel while preserving one load, one square, and one normalized store per element, reducing reduction and synchronization work in a kernel holding 6.81% of device time.

surface: ggml/src/ggml-cuda/vecdotq.cuh Q6_K x Q8_1 MMVQ decode path
statement: In vec_dot_q6_K_q8_1_impl_vmmq, decode each shared Q6_K scale once per participating lane subgroup and broadcast it to the lanes consuming the same metadata, replacing duplicated scale loads, sign extensions, and index arithmetic while leaving quantization types and dot-product order unchanged. This targets the two type-14 mul_mat_vec_q kernels totaling 17.51% of decode device time; the prior experiment drifted and therefore did not resolve the mechanism.

Restore the preserved sidecar mechanism so Q8_1 block sums are materialized once per activation tile and reused across Q4_K rows by vec_dot_q4_K_q8_1_impl_vmmq, removing repeated block_q8_1::ds loads and half-to-float conversions while leaving activation types and guarded correction-lane semantics unchanged.

In quantize_q8_1_1d, replace only the terminal gfx90a ds_swizzle XOR-16 exchange with its DPP row-broadcast equivalent, while retaining the existing offsets 1/2/4/8 operations, the same final FP32 operands and addition, and the lane-0 sidecar writer. This removes one LDS-backed cross-lane exchange from the profile's largest kernel without changing the FP32 reduction tree. Re-run the preserved mechanism because its prior +0.996% result was invalidated by arm drift, not by a measured null.

In quantize_q8_1_1d, replace the terminal gfx90a ds_swizzle exchange in the FP32 sidecar-sum reduction with the previously authored DPP terminal exchange, preserving the existing pairwise addition tree and leaving amax, quantized values, activation types, and dispatch unchanged. This removes a shared-LDS cross-row operation from the top 16.66% decode hotspot.

Map each wave64 to eight independent 8-lane subwaves, with every lane loading four activation values and each subwave quantizing one 32-value Q8_1 block; this increases blocks completed per wave and should reduce the 16.66% quantization hotspot by amortizing wave and dispatch overhead.

Specialize quantize_q8_1_1d for gfx90a so each 64-lane wave is partitioned into eight independent 8-lane subwaves; each lane loads and quantizes four contiguous values, while width-8 reductions compute one Q8_1 block's absolute maximum and sum. This quantizes eight 32-element blocks per wave, increasing lane utilization and amortizing indexing and launch work in the profile's largest kernel.

Remap rope_neox so lanes in a wave process the same rotary coordinate across multiple heads: one lane computes the shared angle and sincos pair for each token-coordinate, then broadcasts them with wave shuffles. This removes redundant transcendental evaluations while preserving the existing per-element rotation arithmetic and output types.

Specialize quantize_q8_1_1d for Q6_K MMVQ consumers so it computes the Q8_1 scale and quantized bytes but skips the block-sum reduction, writing zero to the otherwise unused sum field. Q6_K dot products use only the Q8_1 scale, unlike Q4_K's minimum correction, so this removes reduction and packing work from the profile's largest kernel without changing activation type or Q6_K numerics.

Add a gfx90a fixed-width rms_norm_f32 specialization for 1536-element rows using 256 threads instead of 384. Each thread processes six elements with float4-plus-float2 loads while preserving float accumulation, epsilon, scale, and output type; four wave64 waves map directly to the MI210 CU's four SIMDs and reduce wave-level reduction and scheduling work in the 6.67% RMSNorm route.

Widen the gfx90a rope_neox launch from 4 to 8 heads per position and evaluate rope_yarn once per eight-head group, using ds_bpermute to broadcast sin/cos across the two four-lane quads. This halves the remaining transcendental evaluations while preserving one thread per output pair.

In quantize_q8_1_1d, keep the existing one-xi-per-lane mapping and the existing float absmax and sum reductions unchanged, then use quad-permute DPP operations after int8 conversion to gather four adjacent lanes' quantized bytes into the quad leader; only that leader performs one aligned uint32_t store instead of four scalar byte stores. This preserves every q byte and ds.y exactly because packing occurs after the unchanged reductions and rounding, while reducing output-store instructions 4x in a kernel accounting for 13.84% of device time.

For Q4_K MMQ with ne11=8 on gfx90a, select the existing fixed output-tile schedule instead of Stream-K, eliminating the global partial-sum workspace and stream_k_fixup launch whose synchronization overhead outweighs load balancing at this narrow width.

surface: ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmvq.cu Q4_K small-batch decode dispatch at ne11=8
statement: Change ggml_cuda_should_use_mmvq() so gfx90a Q4_K decode at ne11=8 selects MMVQ instead of the current MMQ plus stream_k_fixup path. The current champion regresses decisively only at width 8, where MMQ and its fixup consume about 46% of device time; a CDNA2-specific crossover can remove that overhead while leaving widths 1 and 2 unchanged.

In dequantize_block_q4_K<half>, decode each packed Q4_K scale/min pair once per 8-lane weight group and distribute the exact integer values with wave shuffles, replacing redundant per-lane packed-scale extraction while leaving quant type selection and dequant arithmetic unchanged.

Restrict the champion's two-partition-collapse launch policy to the flash_attn_ext_vec cases it was designed for, and restore the pre-champion partition geometry for flash_attn_ext_f16 when ne11 == 8; this should remove shared-dispatch leakage into the regressed dec-b8 path while preserving the kept batch-1 attention win.

On gfx90a at ne11=8, dispatch flash_attn_ext_f16 with a 16-row query tile instead of the observed 32-row tile. This is the first width where the champion uses the WMMA f16 path, and its current <128,32,4,64> launch leaves 24 of 32 query rows inactive; the Q=16 specialization should halve masked-row score work and reduce LDS/register pressure.

For dense dec-b8 stream-K only, fuse fixup into mul_mat_q: count only contributors with block_start < block_stop, have each contributor publish its partial to global scratch with release ordering, and use the completion atomic's returned ticket to elect the actual last-arriving workgroup. That workgroup performs an acquire, reloads the other contributors' partials, adds its own register-resident partial, and writes dst; no workgroup spins. Gate MUL_MAT_ID out explicitly rather than treating ncols_dst == 8 as sufficient. This preserves the required inter-workgroup scratch traffic but removes the standalone fixup dispatch and avoids reloading the elected workgroup's own partial.

In fattn-wmma-f16.cu, apply a reversible gfx90a-specific XOR swizzle to the 32-bit-word column index of the KQ and VKQ LDS intermediates, keyed by the row's low three bits, on every matching write and read. Unlike the rejected row rotation, this changes the low bank bits across gfx90a's eight phase cliques while preserving values and the existing MFMA fragment layout, reducing LDS bank serialization in the 11.56%-share flash-attention kernel.

Vectorize convert_unary<float, __half> so each thread loads two adjacent float values, performs lane-identical fp32-to-f16 conversions, and emits one packed half2 store; this reduces address arithmetic and global-memory instruction count in the 9.22% conversion slice without changing type selection or rounding semantics.

Specialize dequantize_block_q4_K<__half> in dequantize.cu to convert adjacent reconstructed values with packed half2 operations and write them through aligned half2 stores. This preserves the existing scale, minimum, indexing, quant type, and dispatch while reducing conversion and store instructions in the 15.18%-share Q4_K dequantization kernel.

Keep each QK MFMA score fragment register-resident through scaling, masking, row reduction, and exponentiation, then consume the resulting fragment directly in the PV MFMA instead of writing and reloading the score tile through LDS. The existing gfx90a MFMA fragment layout already matches the required 16x16 layout, so this removes LDS traffic and barriers from the 11.32% pp512 flash-attention kernel without changing its arithmetic or dispatch.

In flash_attn_ext_f16, keep each normalized 16x16 attention-probability subtile in the existing MFMA-compatible tile<16,16> VGPR fragment and consume it directly in the P*V MFMA, removing the intervening LDS store, reload, and barrier. The fragment layout already matches gfx90a MFMA operands, so this should reduce synchronization and LDS traffic in the 11.32% prefill hotspot.

For the gfx90a D=128 rocWMMA prefill specialization, populate the Q_b MFMA fragments directly from Q_f with the established lane-to-fragment mapping and the same float-to-half conversion. This removes the current Q_f -> shared KQ -> Q_b round-trip and its two workgroup barriers without changing the half bits consumed by the matrix operations.

Route contiguous float-to-half conversion through a dedicated 1D kernel that performs the same ggml_cuda_cast<half>(x[i]) but removes convert_unary's runtime fast_div_modulo, nested dimension loops, stride arithmetic, and repeated 64-bit index construction; this targets the 9.22% pp512 convert slice without changing values or type selection.

On the live production trace, Q8_0 prefill at ne11=512 runs the dequantize-to-global chain: dequantize_block_q8_0_f16 (10.66%, 992 calls) + convert_unary<float,__half> (3.86%, 992 calls) + ~62% f16 Tensile GEMMs - roughly 77% of device time. The chain is chosen by our own dispatcher: ggml_cuda_should_use_mmq() returns false for Q8_0 at pp512 on CDNA2, so every weight block is unpacked 36B->64B f16 to global and re-read by Tensile (weights cross DRAM ~2.7x: 36B read + 64B write + 64B re-read), and the two helper passes cost 14.5% on top. MMQ (mul_mat_q<Q8_0>) reads the quantized blocks once and dequantizes in-kernel into the accumulate path, deleting the materialization round-trip and both helper kernels. This is NOT the answered AK-H-MMQ-1 null: that trace and FORCE_MMQ result are Q4_K screen-rung facts (explicitly rung-tagged non-transferable - Q8_0 never reaches the :309 Q4_K||Q5_K test, and its branch of the dispatch has never been traced for CDNA2 at pp shapes), and the run-23 family proves dispatch-level crossover changes are a real keep source on this silicon. Mechanism is dispatch-only, zero numerics change, so the oracle is the ordinary one. Precondition probe (free, before GPU spend): confirm mul_mat_q<Q8_0> is instantiated under HOUSE_GPU_RECIPE (MMQ_MFMA build flag is a settled, separate question - this proposal does not flip it, it asks whether the dispatcher hands pp512 Q8_0 work to the MMQ kernels this build already contains; if the build has no Q8_0 MMQ instantiation at all, record that bounded answer and stop).

In the current champion (cabac2563), `ggml_cuda_should_use_mmvq()` (ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmvq.cu:660) routes CDNA2/Q8_0 decode to MMVQ only at ne11<=4; speculative/MTP verify widths ne11 in {5..8} - including n-max 8, the measured-best MTP width on this hardware - fall to `mul_mat_q` (MMQ). MMQ at these widths runs the fixed J=8 stream-k tile shape that the kept Q8_0 dec-b4 route (b0eb4fab4, +23.339%) measured at ~29% HBM bandwidth at ne11=4 (occupancy-1, 128-row tiles); at true ne11=8 the J-padding waste disappears, but the occupancy-1 tile shape remains. The MMVQ ncols_dst=5..8 templates are compile-dead on CDNA2 for Q8_0 today; they share each HBM weight-block read across 5..8 register accumulators - the mechanism run 23's Q4_K keep (7d2ea88b) validated up to ne11=8 for the K-quant family - and use the same dp4a `vec_dot_q8_0_q8_1` math that the oracle passed at ne11<=4. Upstream never crosses Q8_0 decode to MMQ on any arch (MVQ everywhere, seed 10); our ne11=4 crossover predates the MMVQ improvements kept since (b1 nwarps=4/rpb=4, b4 rpb=4, y-stream amortize) while MMQ itself has not changed, so the crossover must be re-measured with the current kernel set. Change: raise the CDNA2 Q8_0 ceiling from `ne11 <= 4` to `ne11 <= MMVQ_MAX_BATCH_SIZE` (8). One routing constant; the kept ne11<=4 behavior and all kernel bodies are untouched, so numerics risk is limited to the ordinary oracle tolerance (same dot math as the validated b1-b4 path; MMVQ-vs-MMQ is non-bit-exact but both pass test-backend-ops). Expected effect is honestly smaller than b4's +23.3% (no J-padding at true-8) and the ncols>4 template geometry (nwarps=1, rpb=2) has never been measured for Q8_0 on CDNA2 - which is exactly why this is a bet with a falsifier, not a claim.

symbol: mul_mat_vec_q (ncols_dst=1 Q8_0 small_k instantiation; host forcing in mul_mat_vec_q_switch_ncols_dst)
statement: Extend the kept bs=1 dense Q8_0 CDNA2 GEMV (cabac2563: small_k forced, rows_per_cuda_block = nwarps = 4, +1.508% tg128) from 4 to 8 rows per CTA WITHOUT raising rows_per_thread, by pairing two independent 256-thread 4-row groups inside one 512-thread block (warps 0-3 own rows 0-3, warps 4-7 own rows 4-7) and staging the shared q8_1 activation row into LDS once per CTA (5.76 KB at ne00=5120, padded). The measured-positive mechanism of the 4-row keep is the per-CTA q8_1 y re-read: y is ~1.06x of a row's weight bytes per row at rows_per_cuda_block=1 (mmvq.cu comment on the keep), 0.27x at 4; this halves it to 0.13x of weight bytes per output row and halves CTA count per op (launch/retire tail). Rows stay independent; each 4-row group keeps the exact K mapping (kbx0 = tid/4 over 256 lanes), per-thread 4-row accumulator structure, 3-warp cross-warp reduction and epilogue of the kept kernel, and only the y source changes from per-thread global (L1/L2, CSE'd across the 4 rows) to one cooperative LDS fill read by both groups, so every per-row accumulation order is unchanged: bit-identical by construction. VGPR/thread is unchanged from the kept 4-row kernel (still 4 accumulators + 4-row unrolled weight window), so the nwarps=8 failure mode recorded at mmvq.cu:716 (rows_per_thread=8 register blowup, 'reduction-overhead-bound') does not recur; the risk to falsify is the occupancy side: a 512-thread CTA must keep >= the resident waves/SIMD of the 256-thread one (measured via llvm-objdump VGPR + occupancy, per the 64-VGPR-knee discipline). Change locus: a rows_per_cuda_block=8/512-thread instantiation path in mul_mat_vec_q (mmvq.cu:999-1407, rows_per_cuda_block/rows_per_thread decoupling + LDS y staging) gated in mul_mat_vec_q_switch_ncols_dst next to the cabac2563 forcing (mmvq.cu:1697-1712) to CDNA2 + Q8_0 + ncols_dst==1 + !has_ids + nrows_x%8==0, rpb=4 fallback otherwise. Host-side checks stay in lockstep with the template constants (the run-9 'launch-grid mismatch' hazard).

Generalize the kept Q4_K ncols_dst=4 weight-block hoist (732389d6d, +13.930% dec-b4) to the ncols_dst=8 instantiation of mul_mat_vec_q (mmvq.cu k-loop, line ~1226): the generic ncols_dst>1 path still executes vec_dot_q4_K_q8_1 once per (column, row), re-loading and re-unpacking the same block_q4_K (q nibble shifts, perm scale broadcast, dm) 8 times per k-iter for 8 output columns, where the b4 path hoists it into a q4_K_b4_weight-style register struct loaded once per (row, k-block) and dots it against all columns. At ncols_dst=8 the redundancy is 2x the b4 case (8 vs 4 columns), on the dec-b8 width the champion routes to this exact template since 7d2ea88b and whose kernel body no keep has touched; dec-b8 is MTP n-max-8 verify, the width where the champion historically regressed (-1.462%). Numerics unchanged (same dp4a accumulation order per column); risk is register pressure from the wider struct (16 q + 8 sc + 8 m + dm ~33 regs) at the 64-thread rpb=2 geometry, which the guard surfaces catch.

symbol: mul_mat_vec_q (dense b1 small_k instantiations, fused and unfused; host seam ggml_cuda_mul_mat_vec_q at mmvq.cu:2383)
statement: The b1 dense MMVQ path (mul_mat_vec_q Q8_0 fused/unfused = 76% of decode, plus the Q4_K/Q6_K screen-leg instantiations) consumes pre-quantized Q8_1 activations that ggml_cuda_mul_mat_vec_q materializes in a separate quantize_q8_1_1d launch + global scratch round trip (mmvq.cu:2383-2388). The akm-q8-1-graph-local-reuse keep (+2.1%) already removed the multi-consumer launches (q/k/v share one x). What remains are single-consumer x's (o_proj, fused gate/up, down_proj: ~75% of the 33,505 calls, 4.7us each = 3.70% of device time): for those the scratch is pure overhead. The DPP tree (helpers mmvq.cu:101-189, unchanged by this patch) deposits all four row totals on lane result_lane=63 (mmvq.cu:1551), and the epilogue at mmvq.cu:1551-1594 then runs on lane 63 alone: per row i in 0..3 it reloads x_bias[row+i] and gate_bias[row+i] as four dependent single-lane scalar loads (the champion's own comment at :1563 records that the bias prefetch at :1251-1290, lanes 63..66 one row each, covers only lane 63's own row) and stores dst[row0+i] with four scalar stores (row==0 on this route, row0=4*blockIdx.x, so the four dst addresses and four bias elements are consecutive f32 at 16B-aligned bases; ggml f32 allocations are 16B-aligned and the nrows_x%4==0 gate makes the last CTA fully in-bounds). Mechanism: in the dpp_q8_0_quadrow_reduce epilogue only, replace the per-row scalar tail with vector I/O - when the runtime fusion flags are uniform along the path, two dwordx4 loads bring x_bias[row0..row0+3] and gate_bias[row0..row0+3] into four registers, the same per-row bias-add/GLU/silu arithmetic runs per element (rows are independent lanes of identical operations, so per-row fp order is untouched and nothing reassociates), and one dwordx4 store writes dst[row0..row0+3]; the unfused instantiation needs only the vector store. Keep a scalar fallback when row0+4 > stride_col_dst or the runtime fusion flags differ (uniform per-CTA branch, dead on this cell). This removes ~6-8 dependent single-lane load/store wave-instructions and the per-row reload latency chain from every CTA tail of both instantiations; if the tail is on the critical path (partially hidden by CTA co-residency, which the A/B resolves) this is worth up to ~1-2% of decode.
